map.An area, surface area & volume adventure: This story is about area, surface area & volume. It has five chapters and six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Pattern distortion detected in a set of: Bad patterns found in some blueprints. Reader: get a pencil.
map.Previously: a night-market stall yelled: Last time: a night stall yelled "50% OFF EVERYTHING" and lied. It lied with each percent. The crew found the truth. The pier fund hit 100%. The whole city saw.
map.The city picked OUR design. Skate ramp,: The city picked OUR plan. A skate ramp, a stage, garden beds, a shed. Brightside comes back.
map.The storm flattened this lot. Your bluep: The storm wrecked this lot. Your blueprint fixes it, Mina. You lead the build.
map.We beat one other bidder: Hargrove & Son: We beat one other team: Hargrove & Sons. Their price was too low.
map.Warning: Hargrove's blueprints hum with: Look out. Hargrove's blueprints are bent. Their numbers are wrong.
map.The Brightside lot, day one. Mud, sawhor: The Brightside lot, day one. Mud, tools, and one loud builder.
map.That slanted stage floor? It's half a re: That stage floor is half a rectangle, kid. I'd charge you half. You're welcome.
map.It's a parallelogram. Slice a triangle o: It's a parallelogram. Cut a triangle off one end. Slide it to the other end. Now it IS a rectangle. It is whole, not half.
map.Vocabulary upload. The base is the side: New words. The base is the side it sits on. The height goes straight up to the top side. It is not the slant edge. Area = base × height.
map.To decompose a shape means to cut it int: To decompose a shape: cut it into parts you know. Mina cut and slid the parallelogram. It made a rectangle. The base, height, and area stay the same.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. S: Reader, you are on our crew. Find the size of the stage floor. Beat Hargrove to it.
map.The blueprint shows the stage floor: a p: The stage floor is a parallelogram. It has base 12 ft and height 7 ft. Hargrove says to "charge for half". Find the TRUE area in square feet.
map.Conceptual: a parallelogram is a pushed-: Conceptual: a parallelogram is a rectangle that got pushed. Cut a triangle off one end. Slide it to the other end. No part gets cut in half.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height. Do N: Procedural: multiply base × height. Do NOT divide by 2. That step is for triangles.
map.Shade sail over the stage. It's literall: This is a shade sail for the stage. It is a parallelogram cut in half. That makes a triangle.
map.So same move as the floor… then take hal: So do the same as the floor. Then take half. The cloth bill needs it.
map.Confirmed. Two copies of any triangle sn: Yes. Two of the same triangle make a parallelogram. So a triangle's area = base × height ÷ 2.
map.Noah tested it on scrap fabric: a little: Noah tried it on cloth. His triangle had base 6 and height 8. It came out to 24 square units. That is half of 48. You must do the ÷ 2.
map.Order the sail fabric, reader. Too littl: Get the sail cloth, reader. Too little = sunburn. Too much = broke.
map.The triangular shade sail has base 10 ft: The shade sail is a triangle. It has base 10 ft and height 6 ft. How many square feet of cloth does it need?
map.Conceptual: two copies of this sail woul: Conceptual: two of this sail would make a parallelogram. You need just ONE of them.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height, then: Procedural: multiply base × height. Then take half of that.
map.East corner of the lot. The beds taper s: The east side of the lot. The beds get thin. Carts can pass.
map.Trapezoid bed: two parallel sides — a sh: Trapezoid bed: two parallel sides. One base is short. One base is long. The height goes straight between them.
map.Hargrove's flyer says beds like ours nee: Hargrove's sign says our beds need "double" the liner. VEX does not like it.
map.Trapezoid trick: it's an in-between rect: Trapezoid trick: think of a rectangle in between. Find the mean of the bases. Add them, divide by 2. Then multiply by the height.
map.Mina proved it on the whiteboard with ba: Mina showed it on the board. Bases 6 and 10, height 4. The mean base is 8. So the area is 32. Decompose it into a rectangle and two triangles. You get the same answer.
Liner is cut by the square foot. Find the size of the bed, reader. Be exact.
map.The trapezoid garden bed has parallel ba: The garden bed is a trapezoid. Its parallel bases are 8 ft and 12 ft. It has a height of 5 ft. How many square feet of liner does it need?
map.Conceptual: a trapezoid acts like an in-: Conceptual: a trapezoid is like a rectangle in between. Its true width is the mean of the bases. Use the short base and the long base.
map.Procedural: add the two bases, divide by: Procedural: add the two bases. Divide by 2. Then multiply by the height.
map.Planter boxes for the herbs. Volume tell: Plant boxes for the herbs. Volume tells how much soil fits inside. We use cubic feet. Think of stacked blocks.
map.Except our edges aren't whole numbers. T: But our edges are not whole numbers. Now the blocks come in halves.
map.Formula holds anyway: volume = length ×: The formula still works. Volume = length × width × height. It works with fraction edges too. Noah's test box is 3 × 1.5 × 2. It holds 9 cubic feet.
map.Half-blocks still count. A layer of half: Half-blocks still count. A half-foot layer is just a thin layer. Multiply it like any number.
map.The soil truck is idling, reader. How ma: The soil truck is here, reader. How many cubic feet does one box hold?
map.One planter box measures 4 ft × 2.5 ft ×: One plant box is 4 ft × 2.5 ft × 1.5 ft. How many cubic feet of soil fill it up?
map.Conceptual: volume is length × width × h: Conceptual: volume is length × width × height. Fraction edges multiply just like whole numbers. A half-foot layer is just a thin layer.
map.Procedural: multiply 4 × 2.5 first, then: Procedural: multiply 4 × 2.5 first. Then multiply that by 1.5.
map.Storage crates for the tools — 4 by 3 by: Tool boxes, 4 by 3 by 2 feet. Wood on each face. Watch this.
map.She just flattened a whole box. Six face: She made the box flat. Six faces, one flat shape.
map.That flat shape is a net. Fold it back u: That flat shape is a net. Fold it up and you get the box. Add the areas of all six faces. That is the surface area. It is the whole skin of the box.
map.Shortcut: a box has three different face: Quick way: a box has three kinds of faces. Each kind comes twice. Find the three. Add them. Then double it.
map.Two jobs, reader: pick the net that real: Two jobs, reader. Pick the net that folds into our box. Then find the cost of its skin.
The tool box is 4 ft × 3 ft × 2 ft. Step 1: tap the net that folds into this box. Step 2: type its surface area. That is the wood for ALL the faces.
map.Conceptual: a closed box needs 6 faces,: Conceptual: a closed box needs 6 faces. Faces across from each other are twins. They come in pairs. A true net has just the right 6.
map.Procedural: the three different faces ar: Procedural: the three kinds of faces are 4×3, 4×2, and 3×2. Find each area. Add the three. Then double it.
map.City Hall, 6 PM. The council will fund w: City Hall, 6 PM. The city pays for the bid that adds up. Hargrove grins.
map.Distortion source located: that bid. The: I found the bad part: that bid. The shed is 5 × 4 × 3 feet. The garden bed is 6 × 2 × 1.5. Check it all.
map.Reader — paint covers faces, soil fills: Reader, paint covers faces. Soil fills space. Check our true numbers. Then we vote.
map.Boss Gate: surface area for the paint, v: Boss Gate: surface area for the paint. Volume for the soil. Then one last choice. It is all from this volume, at once.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. One lot. The cou: BOSS GATE. Three locks. One lot. The city is ready to vote.
map.The council votes tonight. Hargrove's bi: The city votes tonight. Hargrove's bid: 54 sq ft of paint for the shed. And 12 cu ft of soil for each bed. The real shed is 5 × 4 × 3 ft. The real bed is 6 × 2 × 1.5 ft. Three locks:
map.Honest paint for the 5 × 4 × 3 shed (eve: True paint for the 5 × 4 × 3 shed (each face):
map.Which bid should the council fund — and: Which bid should the city pick? Why?
map.Conceptual: paint covers FACES — that's: Conceptual: paint covers FACES. That is surface area, all six. Soil fills SPACE. That is volume. These are two different questions about the same boxes.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: SA = 2 × (5·4 + 5·3: Procedural: Lock 1: SA = 2 × (5·4 + 5·3 + 4·3). Lock 2: volume = 6 × 2 × 1.5. Lock 3: check each crew number with Hargrove's. What did he leave out?
map.Built from an honest blueprint: 84 for t: Built from a true blueprint. 84 for the stage, 30 for the sail, 50 for each bed. And each face of the shed is painted.
map.The council audited Hargrove's \"54.\" T: The city checked Hargrove's "54." Two faces were missing. He can't bid for a year.
map.New distortion. A vault door under Vexha: A new bad pattern. A vault door under Vexhall has signs on it. To be continued…
map.Builder, artist, this volume's crew lead: Builder and artist. She leads the crew in this volume. She drew the plan that won. She cut a parallelogram into a rectangle. A builder saw it.
map.Crew captain. Kept the build on schedule: Crew boss. Kept the build on time. Kept each base and each height in the notebook.
map.Evidence officer. Audited Hargrove's bid: Proof finder. Found each face Hargrove's bid left out. "Trust us" is not a unit.
map.Pattern hunter. Treats volume like block: Pattern finder. Thinks of volume like stacking blocks in a game. And he is right.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. It can sense bad patterns. It can't do math. That's your job.
map.Base & height.The base is a side; the he: Base & height.The base is a side. The height goes straight up to the top side. It is not the slant.
map.Parallelogram.Slice and slide: it become: Parallelogram.Cut and slide. It turns into a rectangle. Area = base × height. The stage floor: 12 × 7 = 84 sq ft.
map.Triangle.Half a parallelogram. Area = ba: Triangle.Half a parallelogram. Area = base × height ÷ 2. The sail: 10 × 6 ÷ 2 = 30 sq ft.
map.Trapezoid.Average the bases, then multip: Trapezoid.Find the mean of the bases. Then multiply by height. The bed: (8 + 12) ÷ 2 × 5 = 50 sq ft.
map.Volume.Space inside, in cubic units: len: Volume.Space inside, in cubic units. Length × width × height. Fractions are fine. Box: 4 × 2.5 × 1.5 = 15 cu ft.
map.Net & surface area.Unfold the box into a: Net & surface area.Lay the box flat as a net. Add all six faces. Box: 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 52 sq ft of skin.
map.\"A shape never lies about its area. Onl: "A shape does not lie about its area. Only the one who checks it can." — A.V.
map.completed Volume 5: Blueprint for Bright: finished Volume 5: Blueprint for Brightside. You know area of a parallelogram and a triangle. And a trapezoid. You know volume with fraction edges. And nets and surface area.
map.Thank you for building with the crew. Vo: Thank you for building with the crew. Volume 6 waits behind a vault door. It has signs on it.
map.A different ramp deck is a parallelogram: A new ramp is a parallelogram. Base 9 ft, height 4 ft.
map.Check by decomposing: slice the slanted: Check by cutting. Cut the slant end off. Slide it over. Now it is a 9 × 4 rectangle. Same 36.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.The triangle is half of that: 48 ÷ 2 = 2: The triangle is half of that: 48 ÷ 2 = 24 square units.
map.Mina's whiteboard bed: bases 6 and 10, h: Mina's bed on the board: bases 6 and 10, height 4.
map.Area = 8 × 4 = 32 square units. Decompos: Area = 8 × 4 = 32 square units. Cut it into a rectangle + two triangles. You get the same 32.
map.4.5 × 2 = 9 cubic feet. The half-blocks: 4.5 × 2 = 9 cubic feet. The half-blocks count, just like whole ones.
map.Double it for the twin faces: 16 × 2 = 3: Double it for the twin faces: 16 × 2 = 32 sq ft of skin.
map.A different job: paint a 4 × 3 × 3 cabin: A new job. Paint a 4 × 3 × 3 box. Fill a 3 × 2 × 0.5 bin.
Soil = volume: 3 × 2 × 0.5 = 3 cubic ft. Faces for paint. Space for soil.
map.12 × 7 = 84 sq ft — the whole floor, no: 12 × 7 = 84 sq ft. The whole floor, not half. The stage is paid for!
map.You charged for half the stage! The ÷ 2: You charged for half the stage! The ÷ 2 is for triangles. Cut and slide keeps a parallelogram whole.
map.Use base × height — the dashed 7 ft, not: Use base × height. Use the 7 ft dashed line, not a slant edge.
map.10 × 6 ÷ 2 = 30 sq ft. The sail goes up: 10 × 6 ÷ 2 = 30 sq ft. The sail goes up. The stage gets shade!
map.That buys a whole parallelogram of fabri: That is cloth for a whole parallelogram. The sail is HALF of it. Do one more step.
map.Base × height first… then remember what: Do base × height first. Then think: a triangle is half of what?
map.(8 + 12) ÷ 2 × 5 = 50 sq ft. Liner cut,: (8 + 12) ÷ 2 × 5 = 50 sq ft. The liner is cut. The bed is built. Hargrove's "double it" sign goes in the trash.
map.That's Hargrove's 'double' — you added t: That is Hargrove's "double". You added the bases but did not do the ÷ 2. Find the mean first.
map.Average the two bases (add, then halve),: Find the mean of the bases. Add, then halve. THEN multiply by the height.
map.4 × 2.5 × 1.5 = 15 cubic feet. The soil: 4 × 2.5 × 1.5 = 15 cubic feet. The truck drops just enough soil. Herbs are next!
map.Someone rounded the edges down to whole: You made the edges whole numbers. The 2.5 and the 1.5 count. Halves too.
map.Good start — that's 4 × 2.5. Now multipl: Good start. That is 4 × 2.5. Now multiply by the height, 1.5.
map.Length × width × height. Multiply all th: Length × width × height. Multiply all three edges. Fractions too.
map.Step 1 first — tap the net that folds in: Do Step 1 first. Tap the net that folds into the box.
map.Count the faces on that net. A closed cr: Count the faces on that net. A closed box needs 6. Tools would fall out of this one.
map.Check the end flaps: square 3 × 3 ends c: Look at the end flaps. The square 3 × 3 ends can't close this box. It is 3 ft by 2 ft deep.
map.Net A folds tight, and 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 5: Net A folds tight. 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 52 sq ft of wood. The boxes are done.
map.You found the three different faces — bu: You found the three kinds of faces. But each face has a twin. Double it.
map.That's how much the crate HOLDS (volume): That is how much the box HOLDS (volume). Surface area is the skin, not what is inside.
map.Add the three different face areas, then: Add the three face areas. Then double it for the twin faces.
map.Lock 1 holds. That's Hargrove's number —: Lock 1 is shut. That is Hargrove's number. He left out two faces. 2 × (lw + lh + wh) counts all six.
map.Lock 1 holds. Three face pairs: 5·4, 5·3: Lock 1 is shut. Three face pairs: 5·4, 5·3, 4·3. Add them. Then double it.
map.Lock 2 holds. Someone flattened the 1.5: Lock 2 is shut. You made the 1.5 a 1. The half foot is real soil.
map.Lock 2 holds. Volume = length × width ×: Lock 2 is shut. Volume = length × width × height: 6 × 2 × 1.5.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 94 honest square feet, 1: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 94 true square feet. 18 true cubic feet. The city rips up Hargrove's bid. Brightside gets built RIGHT!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
